newsitem.title: UK: Wm Cook spurns Triplex bid.
newsitem.headline: Wm Cook spurns Triplex bid.

text.p: British engineering group Triplex Lloyd Plc on Friday launched a hostile 57.7 million pound ($96.08 million) offer for William Cook Plc, but the steel firm said the bid undervalued it.
Triplex said its cash and stock offer valued each William Cook share at 309 pence -- a roughly 30 percent premium to William Cook's closing share price of 240.5 pence on Thursday.
"We have done our homework, it (William Cook) is fully valued and we will do what needs to be done to achieve our goal," Triplex group chief executive Graham Lockyer told Reuters in an interview.
But William Cook responded by urging its shareholders to reject the bid, which it called opportunistic.
"Triplex Lloyd is seeking to gain control of William Cook on the cheap. Triplex Lloyd is a group of companies. They may need us -- we do not need them," chairman Andrew Cook said in a statement.
William Cook's shares soared 84.5 pence to 325 late Friday afternoon, while Triplex's shares firmed 1.5 pence to 208.5.
Triplex's offer would consist of seven new Triplex shares and 1,350 pence in cash for every nine William Cook shares.
Triplex Lloyd said full acceptance of the offer would involve the issue of around 14.5 million new shares, representing around 18 percent of its enlarged share capital.
It would also require a cash payment of 28 million pounds.
"William Cook shareholders are suffering from their management's loss of ambition and its failure to pursue new growth opportunities successfully," Lockyer said.
But Cook defended his management, adding that William Cook's board would write to shareholders in due course to explain its opposition to the unsolicited bid.
"To claim that we have lost our way and have no ambition is nonsense. We have no intention of letting Triplex Lloyd get hold of William Cook in this opportunistic manner," he said.
Triplex said the deal should add some 1.5 million pounds to profits on an annualised basis, with the increase coming from sales and marketing opportunities, particularly in the petrochemical markets.
On Monday, Triplex reported that its half-year pretax profits rose to 6.2 million pounds from 3.4 million previously. ($1=.6005 Pound)
